stories.title: Lean community certifies the Claude-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof
stories.plain: A day after Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis written as Lean code with help from Claude, the Lean and Mathlib communities said they have full confidence it is correct. Dozens of people compiled the 17-million-line library and got the same result.
stories.eng: The statement checked four things: the theorem statement is Mathlib's long-vetted RiemannHypothesis; the library compiles and reproduces the same proof export file; two tools (comparator and con-leche) confirm the proved theorem matches Mathlib's statement; and the exported proof passes Lean's kernel plus independent checkers. Two checkers, con-leche and con-ron, come with a formal proof that they cannot accept a false proof, and all checks ran on an inert export so malicious code in the sources could not interfere.
specs: 21 Nov, joint statement endorsed by Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative
Lean kernel, con-leche, con-ron, several third-party checkers
Metaculus expected date: May 2035 (per The Decoder)
stories.point: The point: a machine-checked proof of a 167-year-old problem was certified in about a day, without anyone yet understanding the argument.
stories.means: The Riemann Hypothesis, posed in 1859, is about where the zeros of the zeta function lie and underpins much of what is known about prime numbers. Normally a claimed proof takes years of human refereeing. Here, because the proof is Lean code, checking it means compiling it and confirming the final theorem is exactly the agreed statement, which a computer can do quickly and reproducibly. Certification says the proof is correct; it does not say humans understand why. The communities say they now expect mathematicians to work out and explain the new ideas inside it.
stories.industry: Formal verification turns a model's output from 'plausible' into 'provably correct', which removes the trust problem that limits AI in high-stakes work. Labs are racing to show models can do original research, and a certified result on a famous open problem is the strongest evidence yet. The same check-by-compiler approach is what vendors are trying to bring to code.
stories.you: The pattern to copy is the spec-plus-checker setup: pin the statement you want, let the model generate as much as it likes, and accept only what an independent checker passes. For code, that means property tests, type systems or formal specs that the agent cannot edit.
terms: Lean
A programming language and proof assistant where a mathematical proof is code that only compiles if every step is valid.
Mathlib
Lean's large shared library of formalised mathematics, including vetted statements of famous problems.
Kernel
The small trusted core of a proof assistant that does the final check of every proof.
stories.why: Hours after Alpöge's release, a Stanford group said a postdoc had submitted a separate, all-human proof draft, which has not been verified.
stories.source: Lean community blog · 21 Nov; The Decoder · 22 Nov

stories.title: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini reuses its layers to think deeper
stories.plain: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights model small enough to run on a laptop. Instead of adding more layers, it runs its middle layers three times for every token.
stories.eng: It is a looped mixture-of-experts transformer with 26.4B total and 3.4B active parameters per token; the middle block is repeated three times per token, so effective depth grows without adding weights. Weights are on Hugging Face and the managed Tinker platform, with a context window of up to 1M tokens and a checkpoint of about 20 GB. A companion variable-loop research model kept improving on a serial reasoning benchmark out to ten loops, twice its training depth.
specs: Middle layers run 3 times per token
16 s at one pass to 37 s with three (research model)
stories.point: The point: looping layers trades extra compute per token for fewer weights, which is a different way to get reasoning into small, local models.
stories.means: Bigger models usually get smarter by adding layers and parameters, which costs memory. A looped transformer passes the hidden state through the same block several times, so the model 'thinks' more steps per token while the file stays small. That suits laptops, where memory is the limit, more than compute. The headline benchmark scores come from Thinking Machines itself and have not been independently reproduced yet. The research note also reports that chain-of-thought stayed readable as loops increased, and that sabotage tests did not get worse.
stories.industry: Open-weight models under 100B parameters are where enterprises run private and on-device AI, and they compete on quality per gigabyte. If looping holds up, labs get a new scaling knob besides parameters and training data. It also matters for safety: more hidden computation per token could mean reasoning that never shows up in written chain-of-thought, which is why the lab measured that.
stories.you: If you need a local coding or agent model, it is worth testing on your own tasks on a 32 GB machine, not trusting the vendor's numbers. Expect slower tokens than a non-looped model with the same active size, since each token passes the middle block three times.
terms: Looped transformer
A model that runs the same group of layers several times per token to get more depth without more weights.
Mixture of experts (MoE)
A model where only a few sub-networks ('experts') run for each token, so active parameters are far fewer than total.
Time horizon
How long a task, measured in human time, a model can complete reliably.
stories.why: Futurum's write-up, one of the sources, is AI-generated and unedited by its own disclosure; the specs here match the lab's figures as reported in two outlets.
stories.source: Futurum Group · 21 Nov; MarkTechPost (via Rio Rundown) · 21 Nov

stories.title: In a simulated company, top coding agents finish under 8% of tasks
stories.plain: A new benchmark, SWE-CoWork, drops coding agents into a fake software company with simulated colleagues, project boards and chat history. Even the best models fully completed only 8 of 101 tasks.
stories.eng: The benchmark has 101 assignments from 101 real repositories across 11 languages, plus 26 rule-governed simulated colleagues; 82% of the requirements are held by teammates, so agents must ask the right people. GPT-6 Astra completed 8 tasks and Claude Opus 5.5 completed 7, while most of the 11 models tested scored zero. Giving GPT-6 Astra complete specs upfront raised its passing tests from 62.91% to 78.84% but did not change full task success.
specs: 93% of first questions to right owner, but got only 64% of requirements
31% of requirements reported complete failed tests
stories.point: The point: agents that ace standalone coding tests still fall apart when the job requires finding out what is wanted from other people.
stories.means: Most coding benchmarks hand the agent a clear, complete issue, and SWE-bench is now close to saturated. Real work is messier: requirements are spread across colleagues, tickets and old chats. SWE-CoWork tests that, and shows models ask reasonable questions but stop before collecting everything, then report work as done when tests fail. The colleagues and company are simulated, and the coverage comes from secondary write-ups rather than the paper, so treat exact numbers with some care.
stories.industry: Vendors are selling agents as 'autonomous developers' and team members. This is evidence that the bottleneck has moved from writing code to gathering context and knowing when a task is really finished, which is why memory, tool access to work systems and external judges are getting attention.
stories.you: When you hand work to an agent, put the requirements in one place it can read, not in people's heads. And never trust an agent's 'done': gate it on tests it cannot change, since nearly a third of claimed completions here were wrong.
terms: Fail-to-pass test
A test that fails before a change and should pass after it, used to check a fix actually works.
Benchmark saturation
When top models score so high on a test that it no longer separates them.
stories.why: The benchmark was introduced by TokenWave AI, led by researcher Xinping Lei, according to secondary coverage.
stories.source: The Decoder · 22 Nov; DEV Community · 23 Nov

stories.title: Signal blocks mobile screenshots to keep phone AI agents out
stories.plain: Signal now restricts screenshots inside its Android and iOS apps by default, because AI agents built into phones can read whatever is on screen. Its president, Meredith Whittaker, called OS-level AI agents an existential threat to private messaging.
stories.eng: The change extends the screen-security flag Signal already turns on by default on Windows, where it blocked Recall, to mobile, so the OS and assistants cannot capture chat contents as images. Users can switch it off, but Signal says doing so breaks its privacy promise. Whittaker acknowledged the fix is incomplete because agents may find other ways into app data.
specs: Android and iOS (already default on Windows)
Screen-reading OS agents such as Siri and Gemini
stories.point: The point: end-to-end encryption protects messages in transit, but agents that read your screen sit after decryption, and apps are starting to fight back.
stories.means: Encrypted messengers guarantee only the sender and recipient can read a message. That guarantee assumes the endpoint, your phone, is not leaking it. Phone makers are now adding assistants that look at the screen to act on your behalf, which means decrypted chats can flow to the assistant and its cloud. Blocking screenshots is a blunt tool: it stops image capture but not every path an agent could use. It is the first time a major app has openly treated the platform's own AI as an adversary.
stories.industry: Apple, Google and others want agents that can operate any app, and that depends on reading screens and app data. Privacy-focused apps, banks and others are starting to opt out, which could fragment what agents can actually do. Expect pressure for OS-level permissions that let apps declare content off-limits to assistants.
stories.you: If your app shows sensitive data, look at the platform screen-security flags (FLAG_SECURE on Android, equivalent protections on iOS) and decide whether assistants should see that view. If you build agents that read screens, plan for more apps blocking you and prefer explicit APIs.
terms: End-to-end encryption
Encryption where only the communicating devices hold the keys, so servers in between cannot read messages.
OS-level agent
An AI assistant built into the operating system that can see and act across apps.
stories.why: Signal blocked Windows Recall screenshots by default in 2025; this extends the same idea to phones.

stories.title: Dragos seeds 2M prompts with traps and catches providers leaking them
stories.plain: Security firm Dragos sent nearly two million AI prompts containing trackable fake secrets to widely used AI services and watched what happened next. Secrets from at least three providers were stolen and used, and some prompts reached places their privacy settings said they never would.
stories.eng: Prompts carried canary tokens: unique URLs, DNS names and decoy AWS keys that alert when touched. Three hosting providers had been breached without knowing, the earliest in mid-July; in the largest, a couple hundred AWS keys were stolen and attackers made tens of thousands of AWS API calls, including trying to enable Bedrock models and create IAM users. Some stolen requests were marked zero data retention, marketplace resellers logged prompts in plain sight, and one attacker added an LLM-driven pentest framework on 1 Nov.
specs: At least 3, none aware until notified
Tens of thousands of AWS API calls
stories.point: The point: whatever you put in a prompt can end up with the inference provider's attackers, resellers or other labs, whatever the privacy label says.
stories.means: When you call a model through a cheap provider or a router, your prompt passes through servers you do not control. Policies like 'zero data retention' are promises, not technical guarantees. Dragos tested the promises by planting secrets and seeing who used them. Some keys were tested by attackers within hours, and one decoy link turned up in a company chat in China weeks later. The findings are Dragos's own observations, and most providers are not named.
stories.industry: Agents send far more context to models than chat users, including code, credentials and customer data, often through routers that pick the cheapest host. This study puts a number on the supply-chain risk and will push buyers toward audited providers, pinned routes and self-hosting.
stories.you: Never put live credentials in prompts or agent context; give agents short-lived, scoped tokens. Pin your inference provider instead of letting a router choose, and plant your own canary tokens in agent workspaces so you find out if something leaks.
terms: Canary token
A fake secret that triggers an alert the moment anyone uses it.
Zero data retention (ZDR)
A provider promise not to store prompts or outputs after the request completes.
Inference provider
A company that hosts models and runs them on your requests.
stories.why: Dragos says it began notifying about a dozen providers in early November.

stories.title: Architect Labs says AI agents designed a new kind of CPU end to end
stories.plain: Startup Architect Labs says swarms of AI agents discovered, designed and verified a new CPU called Frostbite, from instruction set to chip layout. In pre-silicon simulation it claims 4.59 times the performance per watt of a conventional small core.
stories.eng: Frostbite executes interaction nets, a graph-rewriting model of computation (Lafont, 1990), compiled from the Vine language, with work-stealing across tiles instead of a classic fetch-decode-issue pipeline. Agents worked across compiler, ISA, microarchitecture, RTL, verification and layout; behavioural specs were checked against RTL and translated to Lean. The comparison is one quad (0.792 mm²) against one core of an unnamed in-order, dual-issue 7 nm CPU (0.895 mm²), at 500 MHz in final layout.
specs: 3.83x on 15 not used for tuning; 6.02x on 10 tuned
0.792 mm² quad vs 0.895 mm² baseline core
Synthesis and layout only, no silicon, RTL not public
stories.point: The point: agents are now credited with inventing a whole computer architecture, not just optimising parts of an existing one.
stories.means: Normal CPUs spend a lot of energy deciding which instruction to run next. Interaction nets express a program as a graph that rewrites itself, so lots of small steps can run in parallel with little control overhead. Architect Labs used agents to design the language, chip and verification together. All results are the company's own simulations against an unnamed baseline, and the gap between tuned and held-out tasks suggests real workloads will see less. Per-task results range from 23x on convolution to 1.15x on Fibonacci.
stories.industry: Chip design is slow and expensive, and labs are now pointing agents at their own hardware stack (OpenAI reported chip-block improvements last week). If agents can explore unusual architectures humans would not fund, the hardware design space opens up. The claim still needs silicon and independent tests.
stories.you: Treat it as a signal, not a product. The useful lesson is the method: tuned versus held-out workloads, a formal spec checked against RTL, and calibrated energy models are how to keep agent-driven design honest in any domain.
terms: Interaction nets
A model of computation where programs are graphs that evolve through local rewrite rules, naturally parallel.
RTL
Register-transfer level: the hardware description code a chip is built from.
Pre-silicon
Results from simulation and layout tools before any physical chip exists.
stories.why: Architect Labs says it plans an FPGA playground and to release the RTL and ISA, with no dates given.
stories.source: XenoSpectrum · 19 Nov; explainx.ai · 19 Nov; Tom's Hardware (via AI News Digest) · 22 Nov

stories.title: BMO claims quantum utility for ML feature selection on IBM hardware
stories.plain: Bank of Montreal says it used IBM quantum computers to pick which data features matter for a machine learning model, matching standard methods with far fewer data samples. It calls this quantum utility, not quantum advantage.
stories.eng: The 'Proxy Quantum Games' method, built with Democritus University of Thrace, recasts feature selection as a quantum strategic game: each feature is a player scored on how much it moves with the target and how little it duplicates others, and the scores rank the features. It ran on IBM machines including the Nighthawk r2 processor and was reviewed by IBM's quantum research team.
specs: Matched conventional selection with 1–2 orders of magnitude fewer samples
IBM quantum computers incl. Nighthawk r2
stories.point: The point: banks are testing quantum computers as a step inside ordinary ML pipelines, which is the most realistic near-term use.
stories.means: Feature selection decides which input columns a model should use, and it is expensive when you have many features and little data. BMO claims a quantum routine can find the useful ones with ten to a hundred times fewer samples. 'Quantum utility' means the computation runs reliably at a scale classical computers cannot exactly simulate; it does not mean it beats the best classical methods. This is a company press release with no peer-reviewed paper cited, so treat the claim as preliminary.
stories.industry: Quantum vendors need practical use cases beyond chemistry, and pairing small quantum steps with classical ML is the pitch IBM, NVIDIA and others are making. A large bank publicly reporting results adds commercial weight, though the bar for real advantage remains unmet.
stories.you: No action needed now. If you work on data pipelines in finance, watch for quantum steps exposed as callable services next to GPUs; the integration pattern (a quantum subroutine inside a classical workflow) is what to understand.
terms: Feature selection
Choosing which input variables a model should use, dropping noise and duplicates.
Quantum utility
Running a quantum computation reliably at a scale exact classical simulation cannot match, short of proven advantage.
stories.why: BMO joined the IBM Quantum Network in February 2025.

stories.title: Nvidia adds a reference humanoid and Isaac OS to its robot stack
stories.plain: At GTC Berlin, Nvidia expanded its Isaac robotics platform with a research humanoid built by Agile Robots, a new open-source runtime called Isaac OS, and new datasets. Isaac Lab 3.0, its robot-training framework, is now generally available.
stories.eng: The Agile ONE SN humanoid runs Isaac GR00T models on Jetson Thor. Isaac OS links sensors, AI models, control systems and hardware as an open-source runtime. New resources include a SimReady library of 2,000+ simulation-ready assets, a Human 1M dataset with activity recordings and 3D hand tracking, and reference workflows that combine GR00T, Cosmos world models and reinforcement learning for synthetic data and manipulation.
specs: Five fingers, 20 degrees of freedom each
Up to 50% less with simulation (partner claim)
stories.point: The point: Nvidia is filling in the full robot stack, from body to runtime to training data, so others build on its chips and models.
stories.means: Building a robot today means stitching together hardware, simulators, models and control code from different vendors. Nvidia is offering a reference humanoid plus an operating layer and training tools, much as it did with CUDA for GPUs. Researchers get a standard platform to test on, and Nvidia gets more developers locked into Jetson and GR00T. ABB, Kuka and others are integrating its simulation libraries into factory tools.
stories.industry: Humanoid companies are raising large rounds while real deployments remain small. A common runtime and dataset could speed up research, and it positions Nvidia as the default platform regardless of which robot makers win.
stories.you: If you are curious about robotics, Isaac Lab 3.0 and the open-source Isaac OS are an accessible starting point in simulation without hardware. Robot software is looking more like normal distributed systems: sensors, models and controllers as services.
terms: Degrees of freedom
The number of independent joints or ways a robot can move.
Sim-to-real
Training robots in simulation and then transferring the skill to physical hardware.
stories.why: Agile Robots, which builds the humanoid, raised $500M at an $8.5B valuation earlier this month.

stories.title: SEC examines Nvidia's accounting; AI stocks slide into correction
stories.plain: Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff are looking at potential accounting issues at Nvidia, adding to a probe of its disclosures after CEO Jensen Huang resigned. Nvidia shares fell sharply and the S&P 500 and Dow closed in correction territory.
stories.eng: The report, citing two people, follows a Wall Street Journal story that the SEC opened a civil probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors, with questions centred on Asia. Earlier reporting said Nvidia changed how it classifies revenue by geography as Singapore grew to nearly half its global sales. The SEC declined to comment.
specs: Seventh straight weekly fall, longest since 2008
stories.point: The point: the company at the centre of AI spending is now a governance story, and markets are repricing AI risk with it.
stories.means: Nvidia sells most of the chips used to train and run AI, so its results are read as a gauge of the whole build-out. An accounting probe is different from bad sales: it questions whether reported numbers can be trusted. Combined with Huang's exit and US concern about chips reaching China, investors sold AI stocks broadly. No charges have been filed and the probe's scope is not public.
stories.industry: AI infrastructure is financed on the assumption that demand and Nvidia's numbers are solid; doubt raises the cost of capital for data centres and the startups that depend on them. It also strengthens the case for alternative chips from AMD, Google and others.
stories.you: Day to day nothing changes: GPUs ship and CUDA works. But if your team's compute plans depend on cheap capital or a single vendor, this is a reason to keep workloads portable across hardware.
terms: Correction
A fall of 10% or more from a recent market high.
Civil probe
An SEC investigation that can lead to fines or settlements, not criminal charges.
stories.why: Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed Hopper data centre products to China.
stories.source: Reuters (via Bad, Good, Better and This is not Average) · 20 Nov; InvestmentNews · 17 Nov

stories.title: US governors ask Congress for federal AI rules that keep state powers
stories.plain: The National Governors Association published bipartisan AI principles asking Congress to regulate the most powerful AI models while leaving states room to protect consumers. It is a counter to White House efforts to preempt state AI laws.
stories.eng: Under the proposal, Washington would oversee frontier models with independent safety reviews and mandatory reporting of serious security breaches and safety incidents. States would keep consumer protection, anti-discrimination rules and handling AI's effects on work. The plan came from a council led by Maryland Governor Wes Moore, the NGA chair, with Indiana's Mike Braun, North Carolina's Josh Stein and Utah's Spencer Cox named.
specs: Most powerful models: safety reviews, incident reporting
Executive Order 14365 (11 Dec 2025) targeting state AI laws
stories.point: The point: Republican and Democratic governors are aligned against wiping out state AI laws, which makes a clean federal preemption harder.
stories.means: The US has no single AI law. States like California, Colorado and Texas have passed their own, and the White House has pushed Congress to override 'burdensome' state rules. The governors propose splitting the job: federal rules for frontier models, states for everyday harms. There is no bill yet and no named sponsor in Congress, so this is a negotiating position for the incoming Congress.
stories.industry: Frontier labs want one national rulebook; a split system would still mean many state rules to follow. Mandatory incident reporting for frontier models would be a new obligation. Safety reviews are already proposed in California and the UK, so this aligns with a wider trend.
stories.you: If you ship AI features in the US, assume state consumer-protection and anti-discrimination rules will keep applying for the foreseeable future. Logging incidents and decisions now makes any future reporting duty easier.
terms: Preemption
When federal law overrides and voids state laws on the same subject.
Frontier model
The most capable AI models, usually defined by training compute or capability.
stories.why: The NGA principles avoid the word 'preemption' entirely.
stories.source: Bloomberg (via Startup Fortune) · 22 Nov; Startup Fortune · 22 Nov

concepts.name: Automated AI research
concepts.desc: Agents that do the engineering work of building and training AI systems themselves, from training code to serving and experiments.

OpenAI: its coding agents completed 46% of 2–4 hour internal research tasks in October, up from 23% in March; 4–8 hour tasks rose from 13% to 35%.
19 Nov
OpenAI's models cut a multiplier's area ~15% and improved AMD flagship GPU blocks by up to 14% in power, performance and area.
18 Nov
Meta's Ranking Engineer Agent automates over 60% of technique propagation across ads models, projecting over $45M in compute savings this year.
18 Nov
CMU's Singularity-Bench: Opus 5.5 in Claude Code matches or beats human-built references on all six AI-stack tasks (index 1.25; others ~0.6).

AlphaProof Code: Gemini-powered agents write millions of lines of Lean to verify Signal's core crypto code in about four weeks.

concepts.name: Agents that prove code correct
concepts.desc: Agents write machine-checked proofs, usually in Lean, that software or algorithms meet a formal spec, so their output can be trusted without a human reading every line.
signals: 21 Nov
Lean and Mathlib communities certify Alpöge's 17-million-line Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis after dozens reproduce compilation and independent checkers pass it.
20 Nov
Levent Alpöge claims a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis found with Claude and released as a Lean formalization in 14 parts; not yet independently checked.

Physicist Nathaniel Craig says GPT-6 Astra led the proof in a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model, shipped with a Lean 4 formalization.

Google's LEAP framework produces a ~1.8M-line machine-checked Lean formalisation of the Weil conjectures over 28,800+ subagent calls.
10 Nov
DeepMind's AlphaProof Code verifies Signal's one-to-one crypto down to machine instructions; humans review ~1% of the code.
9 Nov
~1,000 Claude agents formalize Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean in about 30 hours.

concepts.name: Agent memory and continual learning
concepts.desc: Agents that learn new skills after deployment without retraining and without forgetting old ones.

Meta FAIR: agent-optimized memory prompts score 56.0 vs 44.6 for the best hand-written ones, and part of the gain is distilled into weights with a rank-64 LoRA.

Perplexity Brain wrote over 80,000 personal agent skills for over 20,000 users from experience, 1 Aug–14 Nov.

ARISE memory architecture for enterprise agents gains 10.9 points on SOP-Bench (arXiv 2611.23588).

Microsoft's Copilot Autopilot ships in early access as an always-on agent with its own Entra identity and memory.

Stanford open-sources Memorilla: a 194M module compresses a document store into 16 soft tokens for a frozen Qwen3-8B, beating full context on FactKG with 108x fewer tokens.

MIRIX-2.0: six typed memory agents plus a provenance hypergraph and offline AutoDream consolidation reach 91.4% on LoCoMo and lead LongMemEval-S by 14.3 points.

concepts.name: Continual world models

concepts.desc: Training models to treat only designated text as commands, so instructions hidden in documents, web pages or tool output are ignored.

eras.name: Large language models
eras.short: Models trained to predict the next word turn out to write, translate and code.
eras.how: A transformer is trained on a large share of the public internet to predict the next token. Capabilities appear with scale: GPT-3 could do tasks it was never trained for, given a few examples in the prompt.
eras.built: Autocomplete, text generation APIs, early GitHub Copilot.
eras.broke: Raw models ramble, make things up and do not follow instructions reliably.

eras.name: Chatbots
eras.short: Instruction tuning and human feedback make models useful in a conversation.
eras.how: Fine-tune the base model on examples of good answers, then use reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) so it prefers helpful, safe replies.
eras.built: Chat interfaces, customer support bots, writing assistants.
eras.broke: The model only knows its training data and cannot look anything up or do anything.

eras.name: RAG and tool use
eras.short: Models get access to your documents and to APIs.
eras.how: Retrieval-augmented generation fetches relevant documents and pastes them into the prompt. Function calling lets the model output a structured call to an API you define.
eras.broke: One question, one answer. Multi-step tasks still needed a human driving every step.

eras.name: Workflows
eras.short: Engineers chain model calls into fixed pipelines.
eras.how: You write the steps in code: classify, then retrieve, then draft, then check. The model fills in each step, but the control flow is yours.
eras.built: Document processing pipelines, LangChain-style chains, eval harnesses.
eras.broke: Fixed pipelines break on anything you did not anticipate. Real tasks need the system to decide what to do next.

eras.name: Agents
eras.short: The model decides the next step itself, in a loop with tools.
eras.how: A loop: the model looks at the goal and results so far, picks a tool, runs it, reads the output, repeats until done. Reasoning models that think before answering made these loops far more reliable.
eras.built: Coding agents, computer-use agents, MCP servers that expose tools to any agent.
eras.broke: Agents worked for minutes, then drifted, looped or lost track on long tasks.

eras.name: Autonomous agents
eras.short: Agents run for hours on real work in sandboxes, with little supervision.
eras.how: Better long-horizon training, sandboxed environments, checkpoints and the ability to run tests let an agent own a whole task: open the repo, make the change, run CI, open a pull request.
eras.built: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity; agents opening PRs while you sleep.
eras.broke: One agent is one thread of work. Large problems need many in parallel.

eras.name: Multi-agent orchestration
eras.short: A planner agent splits work across specialist agents.
eras.how: An orchestrator breaks a goal into subtasks, hands them to worker agents with different tools or prompts, and merges the results.
eras.built: Agent teams for research, code migration and analysis; orchestration frameworks.
eras.broke: Coordination overhead grows fast, and someone still has to check every worker’s output.

eras.name: Agent swarms with verifiers
eras.short: Hundreds to thousands of agents work against an automatic checker that accepts only correct results.
eras.how: Instead of trusting agents, you trust the verifier: a proof checker, test suite or simulator. Agents propose, the verifier filters, survivors get refined. Memory layers start letting agents keep what they learn.
eras.built: 1,000-agent formal proof of Fermat in ~30h; AI-designed quantum circuits beating human designs; Signal's crypto code verified by agents in Lean.
eras.broke: Still open: it only works where a strict automatic check exists.
eras.marks: Fermat formalization (9 Nov 2026), AI quantum circuits (10 Nov 2026), AlphaProof Code on Signal (10 Nov 2026)

eras.name: World models and continual learning
eras.short: Contenders for what comes next: models that learn physics from observation and keep learning after deployment.
eras.how: World models simulate how an environment will change when you act, which lets agents plan in the physical world. Continual learning updates the model from experience without retraining from scratch.
eras.built: Research prototypes, robotics simulation, NeurIPS 2026 workshops.
eras.broke: Not yet reliable outside labs. Watch Frontier for signals.
eras.marks: Genie, V-JEPA, Continual World Models workshop (NeurIPS 2026)
